p002-u001: Participants must not engage in or take part in any conduct that the RoboMaster RMOC (Organizing Committee) determines to involve public disputes, sensitive topics, offense to the public or certain groups, or other damage to the image of RoboMaster. p006-u001: The RoboMaster University Series (RMU, RoboMaster University Series) was initiated by DJI and is one of the events under the National Collegiate Robot Competition. It is a robot competition and academic exchange platform created for technology enthusiasts worldwide. Since its founding in 2013, it has always upheld the philosophy of ‘giving glory to youth, giving power to thought, and serving young engineers worldwide to become dreamers who pursue excellence and are action-oriented’. It is committed to cultivating and attracting well-rounded talent with an engineering mindset, and to conveying the beauty of technology and the concept of technological innovation to the public at large.
p006-u002: The National Collegiate Robot Competition RoboMaster University Championship (RMUC, RoboMaster University Championship) focuses on assessing participants’ comprehensive application of science and engineering disciplines and their engineering practice ability. It fully integrates many robot-related technical disciplines such as ‘mechanical engineering’, ‘embedded system design’, ‘control algorithms’, ‘electrical engineering’, ‘integrated communication and sensing’, ‘autonomous navigation’ and ‘human-computer interaction’. It also innovatively combines popular presentation styles with robot competition, making robot combat more intuitive and intense and attracting wide attention from many technology enthusiasts and the general public.

p007-u017: Participating teams must follow these principles:
p007-u018: R1 All participating teams must have the team created on the RoboMaster forum by the team’s persons in charge (team captain or lead teacher). Teams that already exist do not need to be created again. When creating a team, complete the team information as required; contact RoboMaster event administration to obtain an invitation code. After preparing the team, the person in charge may invite participants to join using an invitation link. For the specific registration process, see the registration guide. Registration is successful if the requirements in this section are met. During the season, the RMOC will periodically open the participant-list adjustment function, during which teams may change their participants. The information is fixed when the team last confirms its list during the current open period; it cannot be changed after the period closes. Before each event, the registration center will open one final time. The RMOC will use the final submitted information to produce and issue award certificates.
p007-u019: R2 The same participating team must use the same team name in different events. A team name must take the form ‘XXX Team’, where ‘XXX’ is a name chosen by the team. The chosen name must not exceed 16 characters (each Chinese character counts as 2 characters and each English letter as 1). It must not include the school name, an abbreviated school name, the English abbreviation of the school name, the words ‘team’, ‘group’, or ‘squad’, or special symbols such as ‘*/-+’. The name must reflect the team’s positive, enterprising spirit and comply with relevant national laws and regulations.

p008-u001: R3 A participating team must be based at one institution of higher education and meet the personnel role, headcount and identity requirements specified in ‘2.3 Participants’.
p008-u002: R4 In principle, within the same event (challenge), only one team from a school is eligible to participate. p008-u005: If a participating team does not meet any one of requirements R1–R4, the RMOC will reject its registration application. The team may submit it again after making the required changes.
p008-u006: R5 Two schools that do not have their own participating teams may form a joint team.
p008-u007: A. Before forming a joint team, the parties must communicate fully and establish a team plan based on their actual circumstances. p008-u008: B. Once established, a joint team may not split up and may participate only in the RoboMaster University Championship under that joint-team identity this season. p008-u009: C. A joint team’s name must end in ‘Joint Team’ instead of ‘Team’. The joint team must upload to the registration system a joint-team declaration issued by the schools represented by its participating members. The declaration template is provided in the registration-system instructions.
p008-u010: R6 Each participant may participate in only one participating team throughout the current season.
p008-u011: R7 If participating teams fail to meet any one of the ‘Five Differences’ principles, they are considered the same participating team.
p008-u012: The ‘Five Differences’ principles are different team names, different team members, different advisors, different affiliated organizations (such as schools or colleges), and different participating robots.
p008-u013: R8 Provided it meets the registration requirements for the relevant events, a participating team may register for different events in the RoboMaster University Series, including the RoboMaster University Championship and RoboMaster University League.
p008-u014: R9 In the same season, the RMOC treats one team participating in different events as a single entity and handles all event-administration processes together, including material grants, material purchases and participation support. p035-u001: All RoboMaster participants must fully understand that safety is the most important prerequisite for the sustained development of the competition. To protect the rights and interests of all participants and the event organizers, and in accordance with relevant laws and regulations, by registering for the RoboMaster competition all participants acknowledge and abide by the following safety terms:
p035-u003: All participants must ensure that they have full capacity for civil conduct and the ability to build and operate robots independently, and must ensure that, before building robots with products of the event organizer, SZ DJI Technology Co., Ltd., they have carefully read the registration notice, competition rules and other related documents.
p035-u005: During the event, ensure that the building, testing and use of all robots will not cause injury to teammates or opposing team members, referees, staff, spectators, equipment or the competition venue.
p035-u007: Ensure that the robot structure design takes into account the convenience of the robot safety inspection during Pre-Match Inspection, and actively cooperate with the organizer’s Pre-Match Inspection.
p035-u009: The use of fuel-powered engines, explosives and hazardous chemical materials is prohibited, as is the use of hydraulic or other power methods that may cause pollution.
p035-u011: At any time during R&D, preparation and competition, participants must pay full attention to safety and comply with the RoboMaster University Series Battery Safety Specifications. Advisors must take responsibility for safety guidance and supervision.
p035-u013: Ensure that the robots are safe and that their launching mechanisms are in a safe state, so they will never directly or indirectly injure participants, referees, staff or spectators.
p035-u015: During R&D, training and competition, take sufficient and necessary safety measures against possible accidents, such as wearing safety goggles;
p035-u016: prevent control-system failures; remind team members to think through their actions before operating to avoid mistakes and collisions between team members or between team members and robots; prohibit team members from training alone and ensure someone is available to respond to accidents; and, during debugging, use appropriate safety measures in the robot system, such as lockouts and emergency-stop switches.
p035-u018: The participating team that causes an accident is solely responsible for all liability and corresponding losses arising during practice or competition from unexpected events such as robot failures or an unmanned aerial vehicle losing control in flight.
p035-u020: Each participating team must strictly comply with local laws and regulations on flight control. A team’s Aerial Robot flies above the competition field in a designated restricted area inside the venue; this is indoor flight and does not involve airspace approval. To ensure flight safety, the Aerial Robot is connected by a rope to a fixed ground anchor. If an accident occurs, such as the Aerial Robot escaping the safety rope, the pilot must land and stop the propellers as soon as possible; continued flight is strictly prohibited. Participating teams’ Aerial Robots are strictly prohibited from flying outdoors.
